pests.name: Slugs and snails
pests.description: Night-feeding molluscs that chew irregular holes in seedlings and soft foliage and may leave silvery trails.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.description: Small sap-sucking insects that gather on tender shoots and beneath leaves, sometimes causing curled growth and sticky honeydew.

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.description: A fungal disease recognised by white or grey powdery patches on leaves and stems; airflow and spacing help reduce it.

A quick leafy crop with varieties for each season.
plant_references.care_notes: Grow in full sun or part shade in rich, well-drained soil; keep evenly moist.
plant_references.management_notes: Inspect weekly, remove affected plant material, use clean tools and encourage beneficial insects. Confirm the pest or disease before choosing treatment.

plant_references.summary: A root crop commonly direct-sown through much of the year.

A heavy-cropping cucumber with smooth, thin skin and a sweet, crisp flavour. The long fruit is well suited to salads, sandwiches and tzatziki.
Low-growing sweet alyssum used as an edging or groundcover flower that supports pollinators.

plant_references.summary: Sweet basil with aromatic leaves for the kitchen and flowers for visiting insects.

plant_references.management_notes: Inspect weekly, remove affected plant material, use clean tools and encourage beneficial insects. Confirm the pest or disease before choosing treatment.
plant_references.yield_wording: 0.2 kg per established plant over a 8-week harvest window. Total across repeated pickings, not the yield at every picking.
plant_references.uses_notes:
Culinary herb for the herbaceous layer; allow a few stems to flower for visiting insects.
Fresh leaves for pesto, pasta, salads and sauces.

plant_references.summary: Lemon-scented annual herb to about 60cm with lavender flowers; also called Lemon Bee Balm; attracts bees and suits borders.
plant_references.care_notes: Raise seedlings; protect from slugs, snails and powdery mildew.
plant_references.management_notes: Inspect weekly, remove affected plant material, use clean tools and encourage beneficial insects. Confirm the pest or disease before choosing treatment.

plant_references.summary: Purple sprouting broccoli with green stalks and small to medium purple heads; continues producing side shoots after picking.
plant_references.care_notes: Sow direct or raise seedlings. Cut heads before flowers open. Protect from aphids and caterpillars.
plant_references.management_notes: Inspect weekly, remove affected plant material, use clean tools and encourage beneficial insects. Confirm the pest or disease before choosing treatment.

plant_references.uses_notes:

Good for stir-frying or steaming; purple colour reduces when cooked.

plant_references.summary: Hardy bunching onion with long white bases and green tops to about 45cm; used similarly to spring onions.

plant_references.yield_wording: 8 flower per established plant over a 8-week harvest window. Total across repeated pickings, not the yield at every picking.

plant_references.summary: Leafy biennial culinary herb, available in curly and flat-leaved forms.
plant_references.sowing_notes: Sydney / warm temperate: sow September–May (Eden mild-climate guide). Sow 0.5–1 cm deep and keep moist; germination can be slow. Calendar refers to seed sowing.
plant_references.care_notes: Sydney / warm-temperate guidance. Grow in sun or partial shade with moist, drained soil. The 30 cm plant / 60 cm row spacing uses the wider end of the supplier range. Add compost; feed only as needed. Planning estimates: in row spacing cm, row spacing cm, feeder type, water needs.
plant_references.management_notes: Protect seedlings from slugs and snails. Allow space and airflow; avoid keeping leaves wet overnight. Feeding and water badges are qualitative care categories, not measured requirements.
plant_references.yield_wording: Harvest outer stems once established, leaving the centre to regrow. Seed-grown plants generally reach first harvest in about 65–135 days. A reliable per-plant weight is not established.
plant_references.uses_notes: Use fresh leaves in salads, sauces and cooked dishes; freeze or dry surplus. Retain a separate plant for flowering or seed if desired.

plant_references.summary: Heat-loving annual vegetable grown for tender immature pods.
plant_references.sowing_notes: Sydney / warm temperate: sow October–December after frost risk, when soil is warm. Sow about 1 cm deep. Calendar and spacing are general okra guidance, not a named-variety trial.
plant_references.care_notes: Sydney / warm-temperate guidance. Use a warm, sunny, drained bed. Space 60 cm apart in rows 120 cm apart, the wider end of general okra guidance. Water steadily; excess nitrogen encourages leaves over pods. Planning estimates: in row spacing cm, row spacing cm, feeder type, water needs.
plant_references.management_notes: Mulch and keep drainage open. Inspect leaf undersides and remove badly affected material after identifying the problem. The light-feeder badge means avoid excessive nitrogen, not omit all fertiliser.
plant_references.yield_wording: Pick tender immature pods frequently before they become fibrous. First picking is generally around 80–98 days from sowing; this is maturity time, not harvest-window length. Yield weight varies.
plant_references.uses_notes: Cook young pods in curries, soups or stews, or roast them. Harvest with care where stems or pods are prickly.

plant_references.summary: Climbing bean with stringless young pods, grown on a sturdy support.
plant_references.sowing_notes: Sydney / warm temperate: direct sow September–January after frost, 2–3 cm deep. A 21-day repeat sowing is an optional planning interval within that season, interpreting guidance to sow every few weeks.
plant_references.care_notes: Sydney / warm-temperate guidance. Install a trellis before sowing. Space plants 20 cm apart in rows 100 cm apart. Keep moist after emergence without waterlogging; avoid excessive nitrogen. Planning estimates: in row spacing cm, succession interval days, water needs.
plant_references.management_notes: Protect seedlings from slugs and snails. Water the soil rather than foliage. Nitrogen fixation depends on compatible soil bacteria and does not guarantee feeding nearby crops.
plant_references.yield_wording: The supplier gives about 80 days to first harvest. Pick young pods regularly for a continuing crop; no reliable kilogram yield per plant is verified.
plant_references.uses_notes: Harvest tender green pods for cooking. Let selected pods mature fully only if saving seed or harvesting dry beans; cook mature beans thoroughly.

plant_references.summary: Climbing bean with scarlet flowers and long pods; can regrow from perennial roots in suitable conditions.
plant_references.sowing_notes: Sydney / warm temperate: sow November–February, interpreting the Australian supplier’s late-spring to late-summer window. Wait for warm soil; hot spells can reduce pod set.
plant_references.care_notes: Sydney / warm-temperate guidance. Provide a strong support and moist, compost-rich soil. The 20 cm plant / 100 cm row spacing and pH 6–7 are general climbing-bean planning targets, not cultivar measurements. Planning estimates: in row spacing cm, row spacing cm, soil ph min, soil ph max, harvest window weeks, water needs.
plant_references.management_notes: Watch for aphids, slugs and snails. Keep roots moist through flowering. Nitrogen fixation relies on soil bacteria; flowering plants may still need potassium, especially in pots.
plant_references.yield_wording: Pick tender pods every few days. Eight weeks is a general runner-bean harvest-window baseline, not a Sydney yield guarantee. Perennial roots may regrow in suitable conditions.
plant_references.uses_notes: Grow for scarlet flowers and edible pods. Cook beans before eating; harvest pods young before strings and mature seeds develop.

plant_references.summary: Tomato recorded as Sweet 1000. The cultivar name is listed by a supplier; the growing guidance here is for tomatoes generally until the seed-packet identity is confirmed.
plant_references.sowing_notes: Sydney / warm temperate: sow August–December using general tomato guidance from Eden’s mild-climate calendar. Start early sowings under protection and transplant after frost risk. Not a verified Sweet 1000 calendar.
plant_references.care_notes: Sydney / warm-temperate guidance. General tomato guidance: provide full sun, steady soil moisture and support appropriate to the plant’s habit. Allow 90 cm between plants and 150 cm between rows as a roomy planning layout. Planning estimates: in row spacing cm, row spacing cm, soil ph min, soil ph max, feeder type, water needs, sun needs, forest layer.
plant_references.management_notes: Mulch, water evenly and allow airflow. Rotate away from other nightshade crops. Spacing, feeding, water, pH, layer and calendar are species-level guidance, not verified cultivar traits.
plant_references.yield_wording: Pick ripe fruit as it develops. Generic tomato guidance suggests about 65–90 days from transplanting to first harvest, but Sweet 1000 maturity, crop duration and yield remain unverified.
plant_references.uses_notes: Use ripe tomato fruit fresh or cooked. The record is kept separate from Sweet 100 and Sweet Million; fruit size and flavour are not assumed.

plant_references.summary: Spreading perennial herb also called Vietnamese coriander or rau ram, with aromatic leaves used in cooking.
plant_references.sowing_notes: Sydney / warm temperate: plant rooted cuttings September–February, translating the Australian nursery’s spring/summer propagation guidance. Protect from cold.
plant_references.care_notes: Sydney / warm-temperate guidance. Use a warm, sheltered position with dappled shade and fertile, consistently moist soil. Keep in a container to manage spreading stems. A 45 cm plant / 60 cm row layout is a provisional space allowance. Planning estimates: in row spacing cm, row spacing cm, feeder type, water needs.
plant_references.management_notes: Prevent drying out and keep spreading stems out of neighbouring pots. RHS lists acid, neutral and alkaline soils without a numeric range, so exact pH limits are not invented. Water/feed badges are qualitative.
plant_references.yield_wording: Snip fresh leaves and tender tips once established; allow regrowth between pickings. Repeat harvest depends on warmth and vigour, so a fixed weight or harvest duration is not assigned.
plant_references.uses_notes: Use small amounts of fresh peppery leaves in salads, rice-paper rolls and Vietnamese dishes. This is Persicaria odorata, not a Mentha mint.

plant_references.summary: Vigorous perennial mint grown for aromatic leaves with a chocolate-mint scent.
plant_references.sowing_notes: Sydney / warm temperate: divide or plant September–November or March–April. These months translate spring/early-autumn propagation advice to local seasons. Use divisions or cuttings to retain the cultivar.
plant_references.care_notes: Sydney / warm-temperate guidance. Grow in sun or light shade with moist, drained soil. Keep in a pot or root barrier. Allow 60 cm per plant and 65 cm between rows as a contained-bed planning layout; uncontained roots spread farther. Planning estimates: in row spacing cm, row spacing cm, soil ph min, soil ph max, feeder type, water needs.
plant_references.management_notes: Keep runners contained and avoid overhead watering late in the day. Check for rust and remove affected foliage. pH 6–7.5 is a general herb target, not a measured Chocolate cultivar tolerance.
plant_references.yield_wording: Harvest established shoot tips regularly for regrowth. One contained plant can supply repeated small pickings. No measured per-plant yield or fixed harvest duration is available.
plant_references.uses_notes: Use aromatic leaves in teas, desserts and drinks, fresh or dried. Pinching tips encourages a bushier plant.
